source_admission: Published values the study uses, with how far each was read on 2026-10-18. No outside dataset or full paper is committed; the study's other inputs are the project's committed products (the waters' oxygen, the anoxic depths, climate_targets, the sea chemistry, the springs, geography's drainage and groundwater) and the lake model's own columns. 'read' means the pages holding the values were read; 'abstract' means the abstract or a summary of it; 'secondary' means a later paper or summary quoting it; 'through' names the project study whose sources.json records the reading.

sources.citation: Jellison R, Vignardi C, Melack JM 2024, Mono Lake Limnological Monitoring 2023 Annual Report, Earth Research Institute, University of California Santa Barbara, submitted to the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power, 30 April 2024
sources.use: Mono Lake, a closed soda lake: salinity 69-91 g/kg at 2 m over 1991-2023; meromictic episodes 1982-1988 (6.5 years), 1994-2003 (9.0), 2005-2007 (2.0), 2010-2012 (2.0) and 2017-2020 (3.9), each begun by a rise of the lake's surface of 2.4-8.6 ft (0.7-2.6 m) in a year of high freshwater inflow, with about a 2 ft rise enough at current levels and a larger one needed when the lake was fresher; density stratification from salinity between 2 and 32 m of -2.7 to 15.6 kg/m3 against -0.4 to 5.1 from warmth
sources.access: read: chapter 1 and the section on density stratification and meromictic episodes, with its table of episodes

sources.citation: Jellison R, Melack JM 1993, Meromixis in hypersaline Mono Lake, California. 1. Stratification and vertical mixing during the onset, persistence, and breakdown of meromixis, Limnology and Oceanography 38(5), 1008-1019; Jellison R, Miller LG, Melack JM, Dana GL 1993, part 2, Nitrogen fluxes, 1020-1039
sources.use: Meromixis began with the large freshwater inflows of 1982-1983 and held until November 1988; ammonium gathered to about 500 uM beneath the chemocline
sources.access: abstract of part 2 and summaries; part 1 not reached

sources.citation: NOAA, Oxygen Mooring Observation Network (OxyMoorON), Lake Erie
sources.use: Ten moorings across Lake Erie's central basin, each with six to eight temperature and dissolved oxygen sensors through the water column, logging every 20 minutes from May to September; the scale of an Earth lake's oxygen network for the proposed moorings

sources.citation: Michigan Sea Grant, Great Lakes fast facts: Lake Erie
sources.use: Lake Erie's surface, 9,910 square miles (25,667 km2); its central basin averages about 18 m deep

sources.citation: McBride MS, Pfannkuch HO 1975, The distribution of seepage within lakebeds, Journal of Research of the U.S. Geological Survey 3, 505-512
sources.use: Groundwater seepage into a lake falls off exponentially with distance from the shore, so most of it enters in a narrow band near the shore; measured at Lake Sallie, Minnesota
sources.access: secondary: as later lake-seepage studies summarise it

sources.citation: Abril G, Guerin F, Richard S, Delmas R, Galy-Lacaux C, Gosse P et al. 2005, Carbon dioxide and methane emissions and the carbon budget of a 10-year old tropical reservoir (Petit Saut, French Guiana), Global Biogeochemical Cycles 19, GB4007
sources.use: Petit Saut flooded 350 km2 of uncleared tropical forest in 1994-1995; its hypolimnion is anoxic and rich in methane (above 400 uM) below an oxycline near 5 m, and its emissions fall as the flooded soil and biomass are used up

sources.citation: Paterson MJ, Beaty KG, Findlay DL, Findlay WJ, Schiff SL, St.Louis VL, Venkiteswaran JJ 2019, Long-term changes in nutrient dynamics and plankton communities following the creation of a new reservoir, Canadian Journal of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences 76(8), 1459-1469
sources.use: New reservoirs run eutrophic for their first six to fourteen years, the new-reservoir scenario

sources.citation: Fukushima T, Matsushita B, Subehi L, Setiawan F, Wibowo H 2017, Will hypolimnetic waters become anoxic in all deep tropical lakes?, Scientific Reports 7, 45320
sources.use: Deep tropical lakes are oligomictic; fish die when strong winds bring their oxygen-poor deep water to the surface
sources.access: through lake_oxygen: abstract and introduction read
